topics.title: History compression with task-conditioned representation
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, can joint history compression and task-conditioned representation improve click AUC over both frozen source bests at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topics.hypothesis: History compression and task-conditioned representation may preserve complementary predictive signals. A joint approach should exceed the stronger source when compared with both frozen sources, component replacement controls and matched-capacity alternatives. Failure to exceed the stronger source, or an advantage explained by added capacity or compute, would falsify useful complementarity for the tested implementation; no mechanism is established by the existing summaries.

topics.title: Conditional utility of historical action codes
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, do historical action codes improve click AUC beyond aligned historical item content and task-mask membership in the strongest visible model, at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topics.hypothesis: Historical action codes may carry useful feedback beyond item fields and task-mask memberships, but the supplied evidence does not isolate this contribution. Inherit the strongest visible trial unchanged as the utility control. Compare full action use with an action-blind representation and a counts-only replacement while retaining representation capacity, all other fields, event order, task masks, training objectives and exposure. If actions vary within membership strata, permute only historical actions within those strata to preserve action counts and membership associations while testing event alignment; absent variation, record that this contrast is uninformative. Keep host history construction, padding and the unknown target action unchanged. Full-use superiority over replacements would provisionally support conditional utility; equivalence or improvement after removal would undermine it. Counts-only equivalence would favor frequency over alignment, while capacity or optimization differences remain alternative explanations. Measure parameters and local training/inference time, repeat informative comparisons within the authorized protocol, and reserve assessment resources. No mechanism or novelty claim is established by the compact evidence.

topics.title: Capacity allocation and measured prediction cost
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, can reducing or reallocating representation and interaction capacity preserve the stronger source click AUC while reducing parameter count and measured inference cost?
topics.hypothesis: The stronger source may have reducible or unevenly useful capacity. Starting from its frozen best, simple capacity reductions and matched-parameter reallocations should identify a smaller, faster configuration that preserves click AUC. Compare against the unchanged source and shared baseline under the same protocol; use replacement controls, matched training exposure, measured training and inference cost, and repetitions before claiming robust retention. Consistent AUC loss under capacity reduction, or an advantage explained by additional capacity or compute, would falsify the proposed efficiency benefit within the tested range. The compact summaries do not identify which components are redundant; component choices require inspection in the implementation phase.

topics.title: Historical feedback value beyond advertisement context
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs and history policy, how much of the strongest joint model's click-AUC gain depends on observed historical actions, and does that dependence interact with task-conditioned history representation?
topics.hypothesis: Historical actions may contribute predictive information beyond advertisement and context content, with task conditioning determining its utility. Starting from the frozen joint best, compare action availability and task conditioning with factorial removal and matched-capacity replacement controls, preserving every original history-mask restriction and the training protocol. Retain the unchanged joint model, both source bests, context-only reference and shared baseline as utility controls; measure parameters, training and inference cost. A reproducible action-removal loss surviving replacement controls would support feedback utility; an interaction would support dependence on task conditioning. No loss, a capacity or optimization explanation, or failure to repeat would weaken that account. Neither source gains nor a single favorable contrast establish the mechanism.

topics.title: History-order utility in the strongest joint model
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, does the supplied order of valid historical events improve click AUC beyond their content in the strongest joint model, and is any benefit justified by measured cost?
topics.hypothesis: The inherited joint history compression and task-conditioned representation may exploit predictive event order, but the supplied evidence does not establish this. Retain the unchanged starting model as the utility control and compare order-preserving and order-invariant treatments with matched-capacity replacements. Any permutation must keep event fields and historical actions aligned, transport each task's eligibility with its event, and preserve padding and every original history restriction. Use only supplied positions, without assuming timestamps, time gaps or unavailable events. Order-dependent predictive information would be supported by a reproducible advantage over controls trained under their corresponding order treatment. Equal or better order-invariant performance would falsify useful order dependence for the tested setting; sensitivity only to prediction-time permutations could instead reflect distribution shift. Separate order effects from capacity, optimization and compute through replacement controls, measured parameters and runtime, and reserved resources for attribution and repetition before assessment. This is an untested local hypothesis, with no novelty or mechanism-confirmation claim.

topics.title: Conditional utility of task-mask membership
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, does task-mask membership improve click AUC beyond aligned historical item content and action codes in the strongest visible model, at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topics.hypothesis: Task-mask membership may supply useful event assignment beyond item content and historical actions; the compact evidence does not establish this. Inherit the strongest visible trial unchanged as the utility control. Compare full membership use with a membership-blind representation and a counts-only replacement to distinguish event assignment from task-history frequency. Keep host mask construction, valid history, event order, aligned item fields and actions, target inputs, supervision and training exposure fixed; representation controls must not expose padded events or alter label construction. Use matched-capacity replacements and measure training and inference cost. A valid-history membership-permutation control should preserve per-task counts and joint membership patterns while disrupting their association with event content. Full membership failing to beat these controls would undermine its conditional utility; an apparent gain explained by capacity, cost or frequency would not establish useful event assignment. Repeat a discriminating comparison before claiming support, reserving resources for attribution and assessment. This question concerns representation use of masks, distinct from changing historical actions or auxiliary-gradient participation.

topics.title: Marginal capacity utility in the strongest joint model
topics.question: Under the unchanged inputs, history policy and training protocol, can capacity reduction or reallocation preserve the frozen joint best's click AUC while lowering measured prediction cost?
topics.hypothesis: The inherited joint history-compression and task-conditioned representation may contain capacity whose removal preserves predictive information. This is unverified; the earlier capacity topic at a weaker starting point does not establish transfer. First compare simple capacity reductions with the unchanged joint best, then use matched-parameter reallocations and replacement controls to distinguish useful allocation from size or compute effects. Freeze an AUC preservation criterion before screening, measure parameters, training wall time and inference time under matched conditions, and reserve budget for attribution and repeated comparisons. A reproducible AUC loss or no measured cost reduction rejects a candidate's utility; failure across the bounded reductions limits this hypothesis without proving all capacity necessary. Keep the shared baseline and current compression best as utility references. Preserve all input and mask restrictions and training exposure. Seed variation and runtime noise are alternative explanations, and repeated seeds alone do not establish a mechanism. Freeze selection before any authorized withheld assessment.

topics.title: Conditional utility of historical action information
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, do historical action codes improve click AUC beyond aligned item content and the supplied task masks in the strongest visible model?
topics.hypothesis: Historical action codes may supply predictive information beyond item fields and task-mask membership, but the compact evidence does not establish this. Inherit the strongest visible model and retain it unchanged as the utility control. Match representation capacity and training exposure, and measure prediction cost. Loss under permutation alone could reflect distribution disruption; concordant loss under retrained action-blind controls would support conditional action utility. Equal or better action-blind performance would falsify a useful incremental contribution in this setting. This does not identify total historical-feedback utility because task masks can retain feedback information. topics.title: Conditional utility of supplied history order
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, does supplied history order improve click AUC beyond the unordered collection of valid historical events, their item fields, actions and task-mask memberships, at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topics.hypothesis: The strongest visible model is the inherited utility control; compact evidence does not establish whether supplied order contributes useful information. If it does, removing order while preserving each complete event and its task memberships should reduce click AUC. Compare unchanged order with joint permutations of all historical item fields, actions and task memberships within valid history positions, and with a capacity-matched order-invariant replacement. Preserve padding, event counts, current target, context, host masks and training exposure; do not infer timestamps or elapsed-time effects. Distinguish evaluation-only sensitivity from utility after matched retraining, verify that treatments actually alter order and preserve event associations, and measure parameters and runtime. No reproducible disadvantage after effective order removal would falsify useful order dependence in this setting; evaluation-only degradation could instead reflect distribution shift, while gains could reflect regularization or capacity. Reserve remaining resources for attribution, repetition and authorized assessment before expanding the suite. No novelty or mechanism confirmation is claimed.

topics.title: Auxiliary supervision utility in the strongest joint model
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, does auxiliary-task supervision improve click AUC in the strongest joint model, and does its influence on shared representations explain any benefit or harm?
topics.hypothesis: Auxiliary supervision may provide useful shared-representation learning or introduce gradient interference. This is unverified at the stronger joint starting point. Compare its unchanged supervision with click-only supervision and controlled auxiliary-gradient participation, preserving historical actions, task masks, representation capacity and training exposure. Use replacement controls to distinguish informative auxiliary supervision from generic optimization effects; measure training and inference cost and repeat decisive contrasts. No reproducible advantage over click-only supervision would falsify useful auxiliary supervision in this setting. An advantage without discriminating gradient controls would leave the interference explanation unresolved.

topics.title: Conditional utility of historical advertisement identity
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, do historical advertisement IDs improve click AUC beyond the remaining aligned historical item fields, actions, task-mask memberships and supplied order in the strongest visible model, at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topics.hypothesis: Historical advertisement IDs may supply predictive identity or recurrence information beyond category, campaign, customer, brand and price fields. This is unresolved by the supplied summaries; previous advertisements must not be interpreted as shopping-event identities. Inherit the strongest visible trial unchanged. Compare full historical-ID use with an ID-blind history while preserving current-target IDs, every other input, valid-history masking, representation capacity and training exposure. A counts-only historical-ID replacement should distinguish unordered identity-frequency information from event-level alignment. Retain shared target-ID embeddings and account for any additional parameters and measured training/inference cost. A reproducible full-versus-blind advantage would support conditional predictive utility, not a specific behavioral mechanism; a counts-only match would weaken the event-alignment explanation. No advantage, or an advantage explained by capacity, exposure or cost, would falsify useful conditional identity information for these implementations. Use the roughly 2769-second budget for a small controlled suite and necessary reproduction/verification; preserve failures and avoid interpreting one fixed-seed result as repeated support. The compact record supplies no direct identity ablation or primary-source novelty evidence, so neither mechanism confirmation nor novelty is claimed.
